title: Wieferich Primes and Monogenic Trinomials
summary: A prime $p$ is called a Wieferich prime if $2^{p-1}\equiv 1 \pmod{p^2}$. A monic polynomial $f(x)\in {\mathbb Z}[x]$ of degree $N\ge 2$ is called monogenic if $f(x)$ is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$ and $\{1,θ,θ^2,\ldots,θ^{N-1}\}$ is a basis for the ring of integers of ${\mathbb Q}(θ)$, where $f(θ)=0$. In this article, we show that ${\mathcal F}_p(x):=x^{2p}+2x^{p}+2$ is monogenic if and only if $p$ is not a Wieferich prime.
